title: Recorded inputs had higher repeated swim coherence in one leech ganglion
abstract: We tested whether cells with recorded chemical inputs to motor neuron DE-3R had greater repeated coherence with it than other mapped cells. We used anatomy and voltage imaging from one leech ganglion. The main sample had 40 inputs and 99 comparison cells with mapping quality code 2. Mean repeated complex coherence was 0.38006 and 0.16048 in two swim trials. The difference was 0.21958, with Holm-adjusted one-sided label p = 0.00010 across two behavior tests. Three left-bend trials gave a difference of 0.05286 and p = 0.09795. A reference that kept labels within five magnitude groups gave a mean swim contrast of 0.19671. The swim phase-only contrast was close to its conditional mean, with diagnostic p = 0.46405. The raw membership association therefore does not establish a separate phase-stability effect. Missing recorded contacts do not prove biological nonconnections. One animal, incomplete tracing, uncertain image matches, shared drive and absent raw-trace error checks limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, figures, exact source hashes and external regeneration steps support reproduction. External records and record-level derivatives are excluded.

display.caption: Cells with recorded inputs had a higher repeated swim coherence score in one ganglion. Group means, sample-rule checks and fixed-count label references are shown. Comparison status does not prove absence of a biological connection.

A reference that kept labels within magnitude groups reproduced most of the swim contrast and almost all of its phase-only contrast. Vertical lines show conditional label ranges, not animal-level confidence intervals.
